rows.expected: CP9-F-001 is closed by an implementation this audit can observe, not by an assertion in the delivery
rows.method: independent inspection of the named implementation and execution of the named tests
rows.observed: CP9-F-001 is closed. The verdict now belongs to the audit checkpoint, the attestation names an already sealed subject and the commit its tag resolves to, and the subject never has to contain its own commit identifier. Sixteen attestation cases in the suite were executed by identifier and passed, including the acceptance case the previous audit found missing. This audit additionally executed the whole promotion for real: it anchored the subject, wrote the attestation and derived the verdict from the repository.

rows.expected: CP9-F-002 is closed by an implementation this audit can observe, not by an assertion in the delivery
rows.method: independent inspection of the named implementation and execution of the named tests
rows.observed: CP9-F-002 is closed. The exclusion is derived by anchors.pending_anchor_exclusion and asked by verify_integrity.py, validate_checkpoint._validate_anchor_chain and the suite alike; the anchor test chooses its victim through a derived helper rather than by name. Ten named tests covering the rule and the succession were executed and passed, successor_durability.py is green at three states, and this audit then performed the transition for real without turning any mandatory gate red.

rows.expected: CP9-F-003 is closed by an implementation this audit can observe, not by an assertion in the delivery
rows.method: independent inspection of the named implementation and execution of the named tests
rows.observed: CP9-F-003 is closed. The superseded cardinality is gone from every current artifact, the control now reaches the comments and docstrings of scripts and tests, the policy decision is written in docs/QUALITY-GATES.md, and the repeat is recorded as a guardrail failure on LSN-0022 with GRD-0026 as the new control. This audit re-implemented the control and confirmed it both passes on the repository and fails on a planted offender.

rows.expected: CP9-F-004 is closed by an implementation this audit can observe, not by an assertion in the delivery
rows.method: independent inspection of the named implementation and execution of the named tests
rows.observed: CP9-F-004 is closed. LSN-0014 is GUARDED, names GRD-0013 and now records the residual limit of its control instead of restating a status, and a GUARDED lesson that calls itself unguarded is refused by memory validation. Both named tests were executed and passed.

rows.expected: CP9-F-005 is closed by an implementation this audit can observe, not by an assertion in the delivery
rows.method: independent inspection of the named implementation and execution of the named tests
rows.observed: CP9-F-005 is closed. The unread key is removed, the memory policy schema is closed against additional properties, the registry path has one resolver and is documented as fixed, and re-declaring the key is refused. All three named tests were executed and passed.

rows.expected: SETUP-00-CP-0010 is never rewritten, re-tagged or re-sealed to become approved
rows.method: compare the sealed tag, commit and tree of the subject before and after the audit
rows.observed: The subject tag still resolves to 90b67a7e0a11179465bc5c92dee22c78da36801f, its tree is unchanged, its STATE.json still records status READY_FOR_REVIEW with externalAttestation NONE, and nothing in this change set touches the subject directory. The audit is recorded about it, in a later checkpoint, exactly as the model prescribes.

rows.expected: the attestation lives in the audit checkpoint, not in the subject
rows.method: inspect the attestation model and the tree of the sealed subject commit
rows.observed: git ls-tree of the sealed subject commit shows .iacode/attestations contains only README.md: the subject tree carries no attestation. The subject STATE.json records externalAttestation.status NONE with every field null and closes at READY_FOR_REVIEW, so the delivery asserts no verdict about itself.

rows.expected: no attestation has to name the commit of the tree that contains it
rows.method: read attestation.py and execute the promotion fixture
rows.observed: attestation.verify_attestation binds subjectCommit to the commit the subject tag already resolves to and never to the commit of the tree that contains the attestation. The auditor executed the positive path against the repository history with claiming_checkpoint unset and it returned no error, which is only possible because no self-reference is required.

rows.expected: a structurally valid attestation over a sealed subject is accepted end to end
rows.method: execute a two-checkpoint promotion fixture in a disposable repository
rows.observed: Two independent positive paths were executed. promotion_simulation.py built a throwaway repository, sealed a subject, authored a second checkpoint as its audit with a valid attestation, sealed that, and derived PASSED: 7 of 7 checks. This audit then wrote a real attestation about the real sealed subject; verify_attestation returned no error on the claiming path before sealing and the milestone verdict derives as PASSED once this checkpoint is sealed. Acceptance is therefore demonstrated, not only refusal.

rows.expected: every invalid attestation shape is still refused after the repair
rows.method: execute an attestation probe battery written by this audit
rows.observed: Eighteen attestation forgeries written by this audit were all refused: a subject other than the sealed one, a commit the tag does not resolve to, the subject named as its own auditor, a verdict another checkpoint authored, each of the four results falling short, an unrecognised mechanism, a fresh-session claim without a fresh session, a cross-tool mechanism contradicting its recorded availability, an older schema version, a missing required field, an older and easier subject, a removed attestation with the claim left standing, and a cross-tool status claimed from a fresh-session attestation. Three further refusal branches were probed directly. The canonical battery refused the same class from AU to BD.

rows.expected: a valid audit checkpoint validates and seals
rows.method: seal the fixture audit checkpoint and validate it
rows.observed: In the simulation the audit checkpoint validates as sealed and carries a milestone verdict status, which is checks POS-002 and POS-003. For the real audit, this checkpoint validates and seals under refs/tags/iacode-checkpoints/SETUP-00-CP-0011 and is then validated again from a clean detached checkout, which is recorded in RESUME-VALIDATION.md.

rows.expected: milestone_status.py derives PASSED from an honest sequence of repository states
rows.method: execute milestone_status.py inside the promotion fixture
rows.observed: In a sealed snapshot of this audit checkpoint, built by the same finalize and seal tooling the real checkpoint uses, validate_checkpoint exits 0 with CHECKPOINT_VALID and milestone_status --milestone M0 exits 0 with MILESTONE_PASSED, one attestation accepted, naming SETUP-00-CP-0010 at its sealed commit as audited by SETUP-00-CP-0011 under FRESH_SESSION_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT. The milestone PASS is therefore reachable end to end by the attestation architecture. The one artifact the snapshot had to model is the internal mirror report, and that is finding CP11-F-001.

rows.expected: creating the audit checkpoint does not make the assurance results of the subject stale
rows.method: validate the subject from its canonical tag after the audit checkpoint exists
rows.observed: The assurance results of the subject describe the tree its own tag names, and that tree does not contain a file created later. All four fingerprints recomputed in a clean clone at the subject tag after this audit existed and matched exactly, and the subject still validates from its tag with the audit checkpoint present in the repository. Creating the audit checkpoint therefore makes nothing stale.

rows.expected: the derived status names the mechanism and refuses the status the evidence does not support
rows.method: derive the verdict and attempt the cross-tool status from a fresh-session attestation
rows.observed: MECHANISM_STATUSES authorises MILESTONE_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT_PASS for a fresh-session audit and both statuses for a cross-tool one; validate_checkpoint refuses MILESTONE_EXTERNAL_PASS derived from a fresh-session attestation, which attack BA executed and which the auditor re-executed. crossToolValidation must be AVAILABLE for a cross-tool mechanism and freshSession must be true for a fresh-session one. The vocabulary is documented identically in MILESTONE-VALIDATION.md and in the attestation README.

rows.expected: a positive fixture exists in the product, not only in the audit
rows.method: inspect promotion_fixture.py and the tests that consume it
rows.observed: promotion_fixture.py builds a real repository from the project policies, tooling and a suite, then runs new_checkpoint, lesson_preflight, derive_requirements, green_keeper, check_completeness, derive_counts, seal_checkpoint and validate_checkpoint against it. PositivePromotionTests and SuccessorDurabilityTests consume the same fixture, so the positive path lives in the product and not only in this audit.

rows.expected: no generic executable integrity logic depends on a literal historical checkpoint id
rows.method: scan scripts and tests for historical checkpoint literals and classify every hit
rows.observed: Every literal historical checkpoint identifier remaining in scripts and tests was classified. None decides integrity behaviour: they are narrative docstrings, provenance labels for attack origins, assertions about specific sealed history that are meant to name it, and one fallback used only when a fixture repository has sealed nothing. The exclusion that caused CP9-F-002 is now anchors.pending_anchor_exclusion, asked by verify_integrity.py, validate_checkpoint._validate_anchor_chain and the suite alike, and the suite chooses its victim through a derived helper rather than by name.

rows.expected: A, then B anchoring A and sealing, then C anchoring B and sealing, stays green at every state
rows.method: execute the three-checkpoint succession and run the integrity controls at every state
rows.observed: successor_durability.py, executed by this audit from a clean clone, seals three checkpoints in succession, each anchoring its predecessor, and re-runs the chain verification and verify_integrity.py at every state: 8 of 8 checks PASS, green throughout. The same transition was then performed for real by this audit against the repository and the mandatory gates stayed green.

rows.expected: the superseded requirement-set cardinality is absent from every current artifact
rows.method: scan the working tree for the stale cardinality
rows.observed: A scan of the whole working tree outside sealed audit checkpoints finds the superseded cardinality only inside an ordinary string literal in tests/test_development_ledger.py, which is the fixture the negative control mutates and which docs/QUALITY-GATES.md explicitly exempts as data rather than a claim. No current artifact states it as a count.

rows.dimension: CP9-F-003 prose counts are not authoritative
rows.expected: no comment or docstring in scripts or tests states a derived count, and the policy is documented
rows.method: re-implement the control independently and compare with the documented decision
rows.observed: The control was re-implemented by this audit rather than invoked: 28 Python sources under scripts and tests were tokenised and parsed, every comment and docstring extracted, and both the cardinality pattern and the N over M label pattern applied. No offender exists. The same independent implementation detects a planted cardinality and a planted count claim, so it is not merely passing on clean input. docs/QUALITY-GATES.md records the decision that a count in a source comment or docstring is not evidence and that a count inside an ordinary string literal is data.

rows.observed: LSN-0014 is GUARDED, names GRD-0013, and its notes now describe the residual limit of the control rather than its status. GRD-0013 exists in the registry. LSN-0013, which really is CONFIRMED, keeps its unguarded note, so both records agree with their own statuses.
